description: Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift container platforms — crash loops, OOM kills, resource limits, and orchestration health.
name: Containers & Orchestration
quickFacts: Deploy Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (SCK) to ingest container logs and cluster events.

useCases.title: Container Crash Loops
useCases.value: Containers restarting repeatedly indicate application bugs, misconfiguration, or dependency failures. Crash loops consume resources and never reach healthy state.

useCases.title: Container OOM Kills
useCases.value: OOM kills mean the container exceeded its memory limit. The application is either leaking memory or undersized. Data loss is likely.

useCases.title: Container CPU Throttling
useCases.value: CPU throttling means the container is hitting its CPU limit and being artificially slowed. Causes latency spikes invisible to standard CPU utilization metrics.

useCases.title: Container Memory Utilization
useCases.value: Tracking memory usage relative to limits catches containers approaching OOM before they're killed. Enables proactive limit adjustments.

useCases.title: Image Vulnerability Scanning
useCases.value: Container images with known CVEs are deployed directly into production. Scanning and tracking vulnerabilities prevents running exploitable workloads.

useCases.title: Privileged Container Detection
useCases.value: Privileged containers have full host access — a container escape gives root on the host. Should be flagged and justified in production.

useCases.title: Container Sprawl
useCases.value: Stopped containers and dangling images waste disk space. In development environments, sprawl can consume all available storage.

useCases.title: Docker Daemon Errors
useCases.value: Docker daemon errors affect all containers on the host. Network, storage driver, and containerd errors can cause widespread container failures.

useCases.title: Docker Daemon Health and Version Drift
useCases.value: Mixed Docker Engine versions break image compatibility and CVE patching cadence; silent `ServerErrors` in the daemon log precede pull and run failures. Standardize on a patch channel and alert before…

useCases.title: Container Image Vulnerability Scanning Results
useCases.value: Centralizing scanner output (severity, package, image digest) proves compliance and speeds remediation when new CVEs hit production images.

useCases.title: Docker Daemon Resource Limits Monitoring
useCases.value: Host-level CPU, memory, and storage pressure on the Docker engine starves containers before per-container limits trigger; early detection avoids fleet-wide slowdowns.

useCases.title: Compose Service Health
useCases.value: Docker Compose stacks power dev/stage and edge; tracking service `healthcheck` state and replica counts catches bad releases before they reach Kubernetes.

useCases.title: Container Restart Loop Detection
useCases.value: Rapid start/die cycles burn CPU and obscure root cause; detecting loops early isolates bad images or bad configs before cascading failures.

useCases.title: Docker Network Overlay Issues
useCases.value: Overlay plugins (VXLAN, weave, custom bridges) failures cause intermittent connectivity between containers on different hosts.

useCases.title: Image Layer Bloat Analysis
useCases.value: Large layer stacks slow pulls and increase attack surface; trending layer count and size guides image slimming and base image updates.

useCases.title: Docker Volume Usage Trending
useCases.value: Named volumes grow with databases and caches; trending usage prevents write failures and emergency disk expansion.

useCases.title: Container Resource Limit Enforcement
useCases.value: Verifying cgroup limits match declared `docker run`/`compose` settings catches silent misconfigurations that allow noisy neighbors or false capacity plans.

useCases.title: Docker Build Cache Efficiency
useCases.value: Poor cache reuse lengthens CI pipelines and increases registry churn; measuring cache hits guides Dockerfile ordering and BuildKit settings.

useCases.title: Container Log Driver Health
useCases.value: When the logging driver backs up or errors, application logs are dropped—blinding security and operations during incidents.

useCases.title: Docker Registry Mirror Health
useCases.value: Registry mirrors reduce pull latency and hub rate limits; a stale or failing mirror causes random image pull delays across the fleet.

useCases.title: Container Runtime Security Events
useCases.value: Falco/sysdig/Falco-sidekick style rules surface unexpected shells, sensitive mounts, and syscall anomalies at runtime—complementing image scanning for zero-day behavior.

useCases.title: Container Health Check Failures

useCases.title: Container Network I/O Anomalies
useCases.value: Per-container network throughput monitoring detects noisy neighbors saturating shared networks, unusual outbound traffic indicating data exfiltration, and connectivity issues causing application time…

useCases.title: Docker Exec Session Audit
useCases.value: `docker exec` into a running container is an interactive access event that should be rare in production. Unexpected exec sessions may indicate troubleshooting without change control, unauthorized acc…

useCases.title: Docker Socket Exposure Detection

useCases.title: Image Pull Failures and Registry Connectivity
useCases.value: Failed image pulls block container starts, scaling operations, and deployments. Common causes include registry rate limits (Docker Hub's 100 pulls/6h for free accounts), expired credentials, network…

useCases.title: Dangling Images and Volume Cleanup
useCases.value: Orphaned image layers and anonymous volumes accumulate silently and can consume tens of gigabytes of disk. On CI/CD build hosts this is especially aggressive. Monitoring prevents disk-full incidents…

useCases.title: Docker Swarm Service Replica Health
useCases.value: Swarm services may show the correct replica count globally but have tasks stuck in "pending", "rejected", or "failed" state. Monitoring task-level health catches scheduling failures, resource constra…

useCases.title: Container Filesystem Write Rate
useCases.value: High write rates to the container's writable layer (overlay filesystem) indicate missing volume mounts, excessive application logging to local disk, or tmp file abuse. This degrades performance and f…

useCases.title: Pod Restart Rate
useCases.value: High restart counts indicate application instability. Pods may appear "Running" but are constantly crashing and restarting, degrading service quality.

useCases.title: Pod Scheduling Failures
useCases.value: Pods stuck in Pending can't serve traffic. Usually caused by insufficient CPU/memory, node affinity rules, or persistent volume claim issues.

useCases.title: Node NotReady Detection
useCases.value: A NotReady node can't run pods. Existing pods are evicted after the toleration timeout (default 5 min). Causes service disruption if no replacement capacity.

useCases.title: Resource Quota Exhaustion
useCases.value: When namespace quotas are exhausted, new pods can't be created. Impacts deployments, autoscaling, and job scheduling within the namespace.

useCases.title: Persistent Volume Claims
useCases.value: Unbound PVCs prevent stateful workloads (databases, message queues) from starting. Often caused by storage class misconfiguration or capacity.

useCases.title: Deployment Rollout Failures
useCases.value: A failed rollout means new code isn't deploying successfully. Pods may be crash-looping, image pulls failing, or health checks not passing.

useCases.title: Control Plane Health
useCases.value: The control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) is the brain of Kubernetes. Degradation affects all cluster operations.

useCases.title: etcd Cluster Health
useCases.value: etcd stores all Kubernetes state. etcd problems (leader elections, compaction failures, high latency) cascade into cluster-wide failures.

useCases.title: Ingress Error Rates
useCases.value: Ingress controllers are the front door to your services. High error rates mean users are getting errors. Catches backend failures and misconfigurations.

useCases.title: CrashLoopBackOff Detection
useCases.value: CrashLoopBackOff is the most common Kubernetes failure mode. The pod is crashing, restarting, and crashing again with exponential backoff. Service is down.

useCases.title: HPA Scaling Events
useCases.value: HPA scaling events show when applications are hitting capacity. Repeated max-scale events indicate undersized limits or unexpected traffic.

useCases.title: RBAC Audit
useCases.value: RBAC misconfigurations grant excessive permissions. Unauthorized access attempts indicate potential compromise or misconfigured service accounts.

useCases.title: Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Kubernetes uses TLS certificates extensively (API server, kubelet, etcd). Expired certs cause cluster communication failures and outages.

useCases.title: Container Image Pull Failures
useCases.value: ImagePullBackOff prevents pods from starting. Caused by wrong image tags, registry auth failures, or network issues. Blocks deployments.

useCases.title: DaemonSet Completeness
useCases.value: DaemonSets (monitoring agents, log forwarders, network plugins) must run on every eligible node. Missing instances create monitoring or networking gaps.

useCases.title: Kubernetes PersistentVolume Claim Capacity
useCases.value: PVC approaching storage limits; prevents application failures from full volumes.

useCases.title: Kubernetes HorizontalPodAutoscaler Status
useCases.value: HPA at max replicas, unable to scale, or flapping between min and max.

useCases.title: Kubernetes Ingress Backend Health
useCases.value: Ingress controller returning 502/503 due to unhealthy backends.

useCases.title: Kubernetes DaemonSet Missing Pods
useCases.value: DaemonSet pods not running on all expected nodes.

useCases.title: Kubernetes Job and CronJob Failure Rate
useCases.value: Failed jobs and missed cron schedules.

useCases.title: Kubernetes Admission Webhook Latency
useCases.value: Slow webhooks causing API server delays and impacting cluster operations.

useCases.title: Pod Security Admission Violations
useCases.value: PSA denials block risky pods at admission; tracking them exposes misconfigured workloads and policy gaps before they reach production namespaces.

useCases.title: RBAC Audit Log Analysis
useCases.value: ClusterRoleBinding changes and cluster-admin paths are high-risk; structured audit analysis supports least-privilege reviews and incident response.

useCases.title: HPA Scale-Out Event Correlation
useCases.value: Correlating HPA decisions with replica metrics explains surprise scale-outs and validates max replica settings under load.

useCases.title: PV/PVC Capacity Monitoring
useCases.value: Proactive free-space visibility on bound PVs avoids read-only filesystems and database corruption across the cluster.

useCases.title: etcd Health and Latency
useCases.value: etcd request latency and raft health predict API slowness and split-brain risk; early warning preserves control plane stability.

useCases.title: Ingress Controller Error Rates
useCases.value: Controller-level 5xx and upstream errors isolate bad ingress classes, TLS backends, and canary routes before user-facing SLO breach.

useCases.title: Node Pressure Conditions (Disk/Memory/PID)
useCases.value: Kubelet pressure conditions drive evictions; monitoring them reduces surprise pod kills and scheduling failures.

useCases.title: CronJob Failure Tracking
useCases.value: Missed batch jobs break SLAs for reporting and cleanup; tracking last successful run and Job failures closes blind spots.

useCases.title: Init Container Failures
useCases.value: Failed inits block app containers entirely; fast detection shortens MTTR for migrations and secret-fetch steps.

useCases.title: Sidecar Injection Validation
useCases.value: Ensures service mesh or security sidecars are present where policy requires—avoiding accidental unencrypted east-west traffic.

useCases.title: Namespace Quota Utilization Trending
useCases.value: Namespaces hitting CPU/memory/object quotas block rollouts; trending utilization prevents deployment freezes during releases.

useCases.title: Node Drain Events
useCases.value: Draining nodes for maintenance evicts workloads; correlating drains with pod disruption helps explain transient unavailability.

useCases.title: Cluster DNS Resolution Failures
useCases.value: CoreDNS failures cause widespread `SERVFAIL` and intermittent app errors; monitoring query errors and upstream timeouts is essential.

useCases.title: Pod Anti-Affinity Violations
useCases.value: Scheduling cannot always satisfy anti-affinity; detecting pending pods or topology spread skew avoids accidental single-AZ concentration.

useCases.title: Namespace Resource Limit Enforcement
useCases.value: `LimitRange` defaults and max per-container caps prevent one pod from consuming a whole namespace budget; violations indicate chart misconfigurations.

useCases.title: Pod Disruption Budget Violations
useCases.value: PDBs protect availability during voluntary disruptions; monitoring expected vs healthy pods avoids accidental full service outages during drains.

useCases.title: Vertical Pod Autoscaler Recommendations
useCases.value: VPA recommendation divergence from actual requests drives right-sizing and prevents CPU starvation when recommendations are not applied.

useCases.title: Kubernetes Events Anomaly Detection
useCases.value: Sudden `Warning` event storms often precede control plane or network incidents; statistical baselines catch abnormal rates per namespace.

useCases.title: Persistent Volume Snapshot Status
useCases.value: Failed or stale snapshots break restore RPO; monitoring `VolumeSnapshot` and CSI driver status supports backup verification.

useCases.title: Service Endpoint Health
useCases.value: Services with zero ready endpoints drop traffic for ClusterIP clients; fast detection isolates label selector and readiness probe issues.

useCases.title: Kubelet Certificate Rotation
useCases.value: Kubelet client/server cert expiry breaks node registration and pod lifecycle; tracking rotation events prevents surprise NotReady storms.

useCases.title: Container Probe Failure Analysis
useCases.value: Repeated readiness/liveness probe failures indicate dependency outages or mis-tuned thresholds before user-visible errors dominate.

useCases.title: Node Pool Auto-Repair Events
useCases.value: Managed Kubernetes auto-replace unhealthy nodes; tracking repairs explains brief capacity dips and correlates with hardware or image issues.

useCases.title: Admission Webhook Latency
useCases.value: P95/P99 webhook latency drives API server tail latency; isolating slow validating/mutating hooks prevents global API degradation.

useCases.title: Cluster Autoscaler Pending Pods
useCases.value: Cluster autoscaler unable to scale out leaves pods pending during traffic spikes; monitoring pending duration and CA logs protects scale-out SLAs.

useCases.title: Cluster Version & Upgrade Status
useCases.value: OpenShift upgrades can stall. Tracking upgrade progress and version across clusters ensures consistency and support compliance.

useCases.title: Operator Degraded Detection
useCases.value: Cluster operators manage core OpenShift components (networking, ingress, monitoring, authentication). Degraded operators mean partial cluster functionality loss.

useCases.title: Build Failure Monitoring
useCases.value: OpenShift Source-to-Image (S2I) build failures block application deployments. Trend analysis reveals systemic build infrastructure issues.

useCases.title: SCC Violation Detection
useCases.value: Security Context Constraint violations mean pods are attempting to run with permissions beyond their allowed scope. Could indicate misconfiguration or an attack.

useCases.title: Helm Release Drift Detection
useCases.value: Deployed state differs from declared chart version.

useCases.title: Operator Health Monitoring
useCases.value: OpenShift operators reconcile cluster components; tracking Available/Progressing/Degraded across the full operator set surfaces partial failures before user-facing symptoms.

useCases.title: Build Config Failures
useCases.value: `BuildConfig` runs power S2I and Docker builds; failed builds block image promotion and rollouts tied to CI/CD.

useCases.title: Route TLS Expiry Detection
useCases.value: OpenShift Routes terminate TLS for apps; expiring certs on edge or re-encrypt routes cause sudden browser and API client failures.

useCases.title: Cluster Version Upgrade Status
useCases.value: Long-running or failing upgrades leave clusters on unsupported versions; monitoring `ClusterVersion` conditions and history pins down stuck machine-config or operator prerequisites.

useCases.title: Image Stream Tag Drift
useCases.value: ImageStreams can point to unexpected digests after imports or mirroring; drift from expected tags breaks reproducible builds and compliance baselines.

useCases.title: Operator Subscription Health
useCases.value: OLM subscriptions deliver operator upgrades; unhealthy subscriptions block security patches and CRD updates for platform add-ons.

useCases.title: Image Push/Pull Audit
useCases.value: Audit trail for who pushed or pulled what images. Detects unauthorized access, supply chain concerns, and usage patterns.

useCases.title: Vulnerability Scan Results
useCases.value: Registry-level scanning catches vulnerabilities before images are deployed. Trending shows whether security posture is improving or degrading.

useCases.title: Storage Quota Monitoring
useCases.value: Registry storage exhaustion prevents image pushes, blocking CI/CD pipelines. Monitoring enables proactive cleanup policy tuning.

useCases.title: Registry Image Vulnerability Scan Results
useCases.value: Images with known CVEs in the registry pose risk when deployed. Tracking scan results ensures only approved images are used and triggers remediation.

useCases.title: Registry Authentication and Authorization Failures
useCases.value: Failed logins and denied pushes/pulls may indicate credential abuse or misconfiguration. Detecting anomalies supports security and access troubleshooting.

useCases.title: Registry Replication Lag and Consistency
useCases.value: Replication lag between registry replicas can cause inconsistent image availability and failed pulls. Monitoring supports HA and DR assurance.

useCases.title: Registry Image Tag Retention and Orphan Cleanup
useCases.value: Untagged and old tags consume storage and complicate governance. Tracking supports retention policy tuning and cleanup automation.

useCases.title: Registry TLS and Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired or expiring registry certificates break all pulls and pushes. Proactive monitoring prevents pipeline and runtime failures.

useCases.title: Container Image Vulnerability Age
useCases.value: Images running with known CVEs older than N days.

useCases.title: Istio Mesh Traffic Monitoring
useCases.value: Baseline and anomaly detection on east-west traffic prevents silent degradation and helps isolate failing workloads before user impact spreads.

useCases.title: Sidecar Proxy Health
useCases.value: Unhealthy Envoy sidecars drop or misroute traffic; catching not-ready or crash-looping proxies avoids cascading failures across the mesh.

useCases.title: mTLS Certificate Expiry
useCases.value: Expired Istio workload or gateway certs break mTLS between services; proactive expiry tracking avoids sudden mesh-wide authentication failures.

useCases.title: Envoy Proxy Error Rates
useCases.value: Envoy aggregates L7 failures; trending 4xx/5xx and upstream errors isolates bad clusters and config rollouts quickly.

useCases.title: Circuit Breaker Trips
useCases.value: Outlier detection and open circuits protect the mesh; frequent trips signal upstream saturation or bad health checks that need capacity or code fixes.

useCases.title: Service Mesh Control Plane Health
useCases.value: istiod and validating webhook outages block config pushes and sidecar updates; early detection prevents a widening blast radius across namespaces.

useCases.title: Ingress Gateway Latency
useCases.value: North-south latency reflects TLS, auth, and routing at the edge; regressions here affect every external client before internal mesh metrics move.

useCases.title: Sidecar Injection Validation
useCases.value: Pods without injection bypass mesh policy and mTLS; continuous validation enforces namespace labels and mutating webhook coverage.

useCases.title: Rate Limiting and Traffic Policy Compliance
useCases.value: Confirms quotas and Istio `RateLimitService`/Local rate limit configs actually throttle abuse; drift between policy and observed denials indicates misconfiguration or bypass attempts.
